purpose: Record the c=N multi-stream fp16 recurrent-state decode gain calculation so it does not need to be re-derived. Extends R2 (fp16 recurrent-state quality tradeoff) with the concurrency value that R2 deferred as 'outside c=1 scope'.
per_step_decode_state_traffic_note: Every GDN recurrent layer reads + writes its 3.0 MiB state each decode token (hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/linear_attn/gdn.hip qwen35_gdn_recurrent_rmsnorm_gate_lowp_kernel: recurrent_state[...] read, ns* written back per step). 48 layers x (3.0 read + 3.0 write) MiB = 288 MiB + conv 48 x 0.32 MiB = 15.4 MiB => 0.296 GiB/slot/step.
weight_share_note: In batched decode the ~15.8 GiB weights are read once per step and shared across rows; the recurrent state is per-slot, so its byte share grows with concurrency c.

bandwidth_bound_roofline_fp16_gain.assumptions: decode stays memory-bandwidth-bound at each c; weights read once per step for the batch (native rowtile8 owner / packed AR); other per-step bytes ~2.0 GiB (KV at ~1K ctx + activations + overhead); fp16 halves state traffic (conv stays fp32).

consistency_check.r2_measured_kernel_wall_share: GDN recurrent gate = 1.43% of selected kernel wall at c=1 (post-qmicro decode profile); fp16 halves state traffic -> ~0.7% estimated. Roofline c1 0.8% is consistent.

capacity_note: Capacity is NOT a concurrency lever on gfx1151: 72 MiB/slot x 64 slots = 4.6 GB vs 128 GiB unified. The external's fp16-state concurrency win was a 24 GB VRAM residency story (150 MB/request state); that does not transfer. The multi-stream value here is purely the bandwidth gain above.

prefill_finding.detail: The GDN prefill kernel (qwen35_gdn_prefill_recurrent_kernel in gdn.hip) holds the recurrent state in a register across the whole token loop: float state_value = recurrent_state[state_offset] read once, recurrent_state[state_offset] = state_value written once. State DRAM traffic during prefill = 1 read + 1 write per layer = 288 MiB per prefill (~0.2 GB/s at 512 tokens) vs weight reads ~12 GB/s and compute ~20 TFLOP; even the >1025-token segmented path only adds a read/write per segment. fp16 state saves ~144 MiB per prefill -> <0.1-0.2% of prefill wall. Prefill is compute- and weight-read-bound; the state is register-resident, not a bandwidth term.

caveats: The c>1 numbers are a bandwidth-bound roofline, not a measurement.

MLP/attention GEMM work grows xN with concurrency and may turn compute-bound before c16-32, saturating the gain below the roofline; the c8 rocprofv3 decode profile measures the state-family kernel share to check where the crossover sits.
No retained gfx1151 Qwen3.8 c>1 decode topline existed before the c8 profile; the profile is the first c>1 decode measurement on this lane.
Capacity headroom is not a factor on 128 GiB unified.

c8_measured_profile.finding: c8 batched decode is NOT on the GEMV decode path - it falls back to WMMA prefill kernels for the dense Q4 projections (340 dispatches, 331.7 ms = 81.1% of the 408.9 ms step). Native batch owners cover rows 1-4 only. c8 step 5.52x slower than c1; aggregate only 1.45x c1 (19.6 vs 13.5 tok/s). The bandwidth->compute crossover is therefore not yet measurable; the decode-path gap is the binding constraint.
c8_measured_profile.gdn_recurrent_scaling: 1.776 ms (c1) -> 8.563 ms (c8) = 4.82x for 8x rows; in an uncontaminated c8 decode (~77 ms) the state family would be ~11.1% of the step, matching the roofline's 11.7% state-bytes share. The fp16-state gain estimate is structurally consistent but only harvestable after a native c8 GEMV owner exists.

decision_impact: Quantifies R2's deferred 'concurrency value' as ~6% decode at c=8 and ~10% at c=16 IF decode stays bandwidth-bound. Enough to justify revisiting the fp16-state device change when a c=N target is active, still gated on the full natural-suite KL/top-1 profile and a registered FP32 strict fallback.
